searchText: <@!291925846556540928> I just saw the EIP that came out of this discussion, and it feels very out of place in the EIPs repository. It has basically nothing to do with the execution layer (no changes related to the execution layer at least). It is all consensus layer changes/APIs and how they communicate the current execution layer state. Am I missing something? Is there something that *actually* impacts the execution layer in here? cc <@!554799849288105986> What is this EIP number? No EIP yet, it is still in PR. Here is the PR though: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/4881 https://config.kintsugi.themerge.dev/el/bootnodes Kintsugi EL client's bootnode still working?? anyother bootnodes available for attaching kintsugi?? BLS keygen (and derivation oaths for active and withdrawal creds) had nothing to do with execution layer either, right? It's just a standard related to ethereum <dannyryan> I do get that it feels out of place... let me review and see if I can think of a better home <dannyryan> Isn't that what the eip repo is for? Core EL functionality and otherwise homeless standards? 😅 we have more bootnodes listed here: https://github.com/eth-clients/merge-testnets/tree/main/kintsugi "... and otherwise homeless standards" 😖 This is why we can't have nice things. <dannyryan> yeah, I say that partially in jest (and partially because you know it's true) <dannyryan> on my list to review and see if we can find it a home Thank you so much! FWIW, I think it makes sense to have these in EIPs. <@!301186049323958275> was trying to avoid this can of worms pre-merge, but would it be helpful to have a discussion about how we adapt the repo in a post-merge context?
